:::{#exm-probability-measure}
#### A fair die, and the unit interval

- For one roll of a fair die,
  the sample space is $\samplespace = D = \set{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}$,
  the events are all subsets of $D$,
  and $\Pf{A} \eqdef \abs{A} / 6$.
  $\P$ is the counting function $\measure(A) = \abs{A}$ of @exm-measure divided by $6$.
  So $\Pf{\emptyset} = 0$,
  and $\P$ is countably additive,
  because each sum in @exm-countable-additivity has at most six nonzero terms,
  and dividing a finite sum by $6$ divides each term by $6$.
  It is a probability measure, since $\Pf{D} = 6/6 = 1$.
  The outcome $3$ is in the event "the roll is odd", $\set{1, 3, 5}$,
  which has $\Pf{\set{1, 3, 5}} = 3/6 = 1/2$.
- Lebesgue measure on $[0, 1]$ is a probability measure,
  because $\lebesgue([0, 1]) = 1$ (@exm-lebesgue-measure).
- The counting measure on $D$ is not a probability measure,
  because it gives $D$ the value $6$.

:::
